newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia sees 1998 T-bill yields at 12-14 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia sees 1998 T-bill yields at 12-14 pct.

text.p: Yields on Russia's government securities markets are likely to fall to 12-14 percent in 1998, and the Central Bank's discount, or refinancing, rate will fall to 20 percent, with inflation next year of five percent, First Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov said on Thursday.

Yields are currently around 20 percent, the level to which the Finance Ministry recently forecast they would fall by the end of the year. The refinancing rate, effectively a cap on T-bill yields, is 36 percent, and inflation is forecast to slow to 5-8 percent next year from a planned 12 percent this year.

"We are forecasting a rate on GKO T-bills of 12-14 percent in 1998, a discount rate on our calculations of 20 percent, with inflation of five percent," Petrov told a news conference after a cabinet meeting which discussed the 1998 budget and the medium-term budgetary outlook.

Petrov said the 1998 budget deficit, according to international calculations including debt servicing, would fall to 4.6 percent of gross domestic product next year, and the government aimed to reduce it to 3.5 percent by 2000.
The total deficit in 1997 by international standards is about seven percent. Russian deficit calculation which exclude borrowing costs put the deficit this year at 3.5 percent.
Last week Finance Minister Anatoly Chubais said the 1998 deficit would be five percent of GDP, comprising a primary deficit excluding borrowing costs of 0.5 percent and 4.5 percent on debt servicing.
